title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X_• is a simplicial set (or a simplicial space treated through the topos of sheaves on X_•) and k_• is the constant ring. C^*_• = C^*_{•k} is the simplicial cochain complex m ↦ C^*(Δ[m],k) of the standard simplices. C^*_{X_•} is its pull-back to X_•. F is a k_•-Module on X_•: a family of stalks F_y (y ∈ X_m) with transition maps F(σ^*y) → F(y) for each simplicial operator σ.

The previous pages apparently handled locally constant F (cochains with local coefficients). This page removes that hypothesis in four steps.
(1) Global sections. C^*(X_•,F) ≅ Γ(X_•, C^*_{X_•} ⊗_{k_•} F). Reason: C^n_m = k^{Hom([n],[m])}. A compatible section of C^n ⊗ F is determined by its components s_n(x)_{id} ∈ F_x for x ∈ X_n, and these can be chosen freely. So Γ = ∏_{x∈X_n} F_x, which is the module of n-cochains.
(2) Resolution. C^*_{X_•} ⊗ F is a resolution of F, because each Δ[m] is contractible and C^q(Δ[m],k) is finite free.
(3) Flasqueness. The terms are Γ-acyclic ('flasque', with the margin note 'à vérifier en passant'), whether or not F is locally constant.
(4) Conclusion. There is a canonical isomorphism H^*(C^*(X_•,F)) ≅ H^*(X_•,F). It is functorial in F and compatible with coboundaries. The same holds for hypercohomology with coefficients in a complex F^* of k-Modules, using the total complex of the double complex. In derived-category language this is an isomorphism of triangulated functors RΓ(X_•,F^*) ≅ Tot C^*(X_•,F^*).

The next page studies maps from a complex of (co)simplicial modules A^·_* into C^·_{*M}. It uses the adjunction Hom(A^n_*, C^n_{*M}) = Hom(A^n_n, M): C^n_{*M} is cofree, the right Kan extension of M from level n. The aim seems to be characterising chain maps into the cochain complex. This prepares a comparison, presumably by integration, between the divided-power de Rham complex of the simplices (the subject of cote 136) and simplicial cochains. It is in the spirit of acyclic models.
errors: No mathematical error. Flasqueness, left 'à vérifier', does hold in the simplicial-set case. C^n ⊗ F is not literally coinduced from level n unless F is locally constant. But it equals π_*π^*F along a discrete fibration whose fibre components (x ↓ Δ/X) have initial objects. So its higher cohomology vanishes and H^0 = ∏_{x∈X_n} F_x.
Minor notational slip: Γ(X_•, C^*_{X_•} ⊗_k F is missing its closing parenthesis.

ideas.what: Cochains on a simplicial set with coefficients in an arbitrary (not locally constant) sheaf/coefficient system F compute sheaf cohomology of X_•, via the resolution C^*_{X_•} ⊗ F by Γ-acyclic sheaves.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of simplicial sets / small categories with coefficient systems; cosimplicial replacement; RΓ(X_•,F) ≅ ∏_{x∈X_n} F_x complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Gabriel–Zisman, Illusie (Complexe cotangent), SGA4 Vbis, Deligne Hodge III; later Moerdijk, Baues–Wirsching
ideas.where_published: Close in spirit to SGA4 Vbis (cohomological descent, by Saint-Donat/Deligne), not by Grothendieck himself

ideas.what: The simplicial cochain complex of standard simplices C^*_• as a sheaf on X_•, with C^n_{*M} cofree (right adjoint to evaluation at level n).
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial cochain algebra C^*(Δ^•); cofree/coinduced simplicial modules; method of acyclic models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–MacLane, H. Cartan (théorie simpliciale des formes différentielles), Sullivan

ideas.what: Derived-category formulation as an isomorphism of triangulated functors, including complexes of coefficients via the total complex.
ideas.modern_name: RΓ on the topos of a simplicial set

deep.surprise_reason: Standard homological algebra: cochains with coefficients in an arbitrary sheaf on a simplicial set compute its cohomology. It is a preparatory lemma for the comparison of the divided-power de Rham complex with simplicial cochains. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Top line: 'F sur X_• (pas/≠ loc. constant, un k_•-Module)'. The parenthetical insertion above F is a marginal note; its reading is uncertain.
'vom [?] [-compatible-] fonctoriel en F' should most likely read 'isom. fonctoriel en F'. The struck word is 'compatible', with 'isom.' written above.
'Γ(X_•, C^*_{X_•} ⊗_k F' is missing its closing parenthesis in the manuscript itself.
The marginal note at the bottom likely reads 'pour complexe simple associé aux deux degrés (venant de C^* et de F^*)', i.e. the total complex, rather than 'pour degrés tot.'.
Left margin NB: probably 'NB on a C^*_• = C^*_{•k} si on désigne [?]', i.e. C^*_• is the cochain complex with coefficients in k.
